role: Adversarial reviewer of retained CAD warnings, prior clearance evidence and false-negative classes

directChecks.method: Independent source-port/net disjoint-set identity from source_trace declarations; map every warning to its actual source-owned PCB traces; directly inspect wire widths and declared planar lengths on all 633 traces. No build or board writes.

strengths: The 44 frightening thin-trace warnings do not describe the actual requested source-owned routes; all 633 actual traces satisfy their declared minimum width and 446 bounded traces satisfy their stated planar length limits in a direct reread.

The prior checker resolves logical identity from declared source ports and nets, includes unknown pads as foreign copper, rejects contradictory/unresolved conductor identity, models finite swept widths, and distinguishes same-layer conductors and full four-layer barrels.
Current capture has complementary actual-pour, drill, physical-net and reference checks beyond angle lint; the warning list is retained rather than hidden.

findings.explanation: All 44 pcb_trace_warning rows select a different same-net branch rather than the branch belonging to the warned source_trace. Their 0.20 mm value is a real monitor/control branch width, but the requested power branch is present at the intended width. This warning mechanism should be repaired to improve trust in CAD diagnostics.

39 warning records identify missing requires_power/requires_ground/pinAttributes semantics, including U_MCU ground and U_INPUT power. They are not measured copper opens or shorts, but a zero error count cannot be treated as full electrical-rule validation while these assertions remain absent. Six USB missing-trace warnings identify unused DP/DN/SBU pins, and 19 refdes warnings are naming/type mismatches.

Prior same-capture layout measurement retains 0.34176537829136944 mm² of inherited ground projection support loss under PD_PROTECTED_DISCHARGE_FEED. That is a real return-reference limitation, although not a copper short and not newly introduced by Source23. A routing quality score should not erase it merely because the current revision caused no additional loss.

evidence.measurement: Existing same-capture report, not remeasured by this reviewer

findings.explanation: Long perimeter power and UART detours remain. FAN_PROTECTED_POWER_FEED travels from (16.330079,23) via x=48.8 to its bottom feed; UART_TX_MCU_BOTTOM_HEADER has a 56.079 mm bottom route with 11 bends. Existing style evidence reports 23.646 mm and 23.169 mm obstacle-ignoring detour excess on the respective examined spans. Those lower bounds do not prove an alternative is feasible, but they prevent an exceptional economy rating.

The Source23 all-current pass is a composite of authenticated unchanged baseline geometry plus bounded R206 delta and fresh actual-pour checks. It explicitly does not rerun all unchanged nonpour pairs. This is a defensible incremental verification method if the retention chain is complete; it is not a fresh independent all-pair same-capture DRC. A screenshot allegation should still be localized and independently checked.

Six supplier-footprint mismatch warnings report real IoU differences from the cached supplier footprint. The imported source parts explicitly document in-place datasheet-based copper corrections; they should be retained as documented differences rather than called proven shorts. Three connector-access warnings arise from inferred insertion direction and should be resolved with real connector access metadata. Neither class is a measured copper short in this review.

suspectedShortAssessment.status: No confirmed short identified in retained warnings or direct source-width/length checks. The screenshot region was not independently localized by this reviewer.
suspectedShortAssessment.properTest: Locate actual primitive IDs and physical layer/net roots, then compute swept finite-copper intersection and the required edge gap. Earlier pass claims alone are insufficient.

topImprovements: Repair width warning ownership so it evaluates the actual warned source-owned route rather than an arbitrary same-net branch.
Add explicit electrical pin attributes and deliberate USB unused-pin declarations; add insertionDirection on the connector imports.
Explore shortening long power/UART perimeter detours while preserving ground references and minimum clearances.
Improve the discharge feed reference-plane coverage without cutting the main ground plane.
Bind a fresh direct all-current geometry check to the suspected screenshot region, with reproducible net/layer IDs and coordinates.
limitations: This reviewer directly rechecked widths, declared planar limits, warning ownership and source identities, not all physical intersections.
Ground-support deficit and obstacle-ignoring detour metrics cited above are existing measurements on the exact hash-bound capture.
No screenshot localization, Gerber mask/drill checks, thermal/EMI measurements or hardware readiness claim.
Score deductions concern routing economy and retained return-reference geometry, not the fact that the board is unbuilt.
scoreRationale: Solid prototype routing with strong evidence of intended copper widths and identity, but substantial long detours and a retained ground-reference compromise keep it at 7/10. The 117-warning headline alone is neither evidence of a short nor a reason for a low score.
